question: Why were ancient Greeks told that cinnamon came from the nests of giant birds on cliffs?
answer: Because the traders who sold it profited from the story. Herodotus recorded it around 430 BC: birds built nests of cinnamon sticks on sheer rock, and gatherers lured them with heavy chunks of meat. Five centuries later Pliny dismissed such tales as inventions of the Arabian dealers, made up to raise their prices.
move: When a seller explains why something is rare, ask who profits from it.
ask: Whose story about why something costs so much have I just accepted?
reference: Pliny the Elder, Natural History, Book 12, trans. Rackham, Loeb Classical Library, Harvard University Press, 1945
